title: Real rectangle divergence formula with complex values
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] with product Lebesgue measure. Let $a_1\leq b_1$ and $a_2\leq b_2$ be real numbers and put $Q=[a_1,b_1]\times[a_2,b_2]$. Let $F,G:\mathbf R^2\to\mathbf C$ be continuous on $Q$ and real Frechet differentiable at every point of $(a_1,b_1)\times(a_2,b_2)$. Let $L,M$ assign continuous real-linear maps $\mathbf R^2\to\mathbf C$ to points of $Q$, agreeing there with $DF,DG$ at every interior point. No continuity of $L,M$ as functions of the point is assumed. If $H(x,y)=L(x,y)[(1,0)]+M(x,y)[(0,1)]$ is Lebesgue integrable on $Q$, then $$\int_Q H(x,y)\,dx\,dy=\int_{a_1}^{b_1}\bigl(G(x,b_2)-G(x,a_2)\bigr)\,dx+\int_{a_2}^{b_2}\bigl(F(b_1,y)-F(a_1,y)\bigr)\,dy.$$ This includes rectangles with a zero side length.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: E = C as a real normed vector space, a = (a_1,a_2), b = (b_1,b_2), f = F, g = G, f' = L, g' = M, in lines 482–494. The displayed formula just groups the two differences of boundary integrals; continuous restrictions to compact intervals are integrable. The theorem asks no continuity of L or M, only IntegrableOn of their indicated sum. Non-strict a <= b covers degenerate rectangles.
